description: HPO terms for the 20 ats checklist items (configs/checklists/ats.json), chosen on 2026-11-15 by a Claude helper from the pinned HPO release by name and synonym search and hierarchy checks (pipeline/extract/hpo_lookup.py), D-40 as extended by D-47. 'observed' is the one term a record may assert when the item is observed; null where the item is a composite no single term covers exactly (the free-text feature rows carry the specific term). 'excluded' lists every term a record may mark excluded when the item is explicitly absent. Flagged for review by Jimmy or the panel; not a pre-registered choice.

aortic tortuosity or elongation.note: Aortic tortuosity; exact name match for the tortuosity part. HPO has no aortic elongation term and an elongated aorta alone does not imply tortuosity, so observed is null (as for 'recurrent tonsillitis or tonsillectomy' in the tangier map); only the tortuosity component can be excluded.

tortuosity of arteries other than the ao.note: Arterial tortuosity (children: carotid, vertebral, cerebral, temporal, retinal and generalized arterial tortuosity). In HPO, Aortic tortuosity sits under Abnormal aortic morphology and is not a descendant of Arterial tortuosity, so this term's subtree holds only non-aortic arteries and its absence does not touch the aortic item. Vascular tortuosity is broader (includes veins).

pulmonary artery stenosis.note: Pulmonary artery stenosis; exact name match. Peripheral pulmonary artery stenosis is its child.

stenosis of the aorta or aortic branches.note: Composite: Coarctation of aorta (EXACT 'Narrowing of the aorta'), Supravalvular aortic stenosis (ascending aorta above the valve; filed under aortic valve physiology), Arterial stenosis (systemic arteries; renal, carotid and peripheral arterial stenosis are descendants), plus Coronary artery stenosis and Subclavian artery stenosis, which are not under Arterial stenosis. Pulmonary artery stenosis is not under Arterial stenosis, so it stays with its own item. Their common ancestor, Abnormal systemic arterial morphology, is far broader. Cerebral artery stenosis is left out as intracranial, not an aortic branch.

aortic root aneurysm.note: Aortic root aneurysm; exact name match (EXACT synonyms 'Enlarged aortic root', 'Increased aortic root diameter'; synonym 'Aortic root dilatation').

arterial dissection.note: Arterial dissection; exact name match. In HPO, Aortic dissection, Carotid artery dissection, Coronary artery dissection and Celiac artery dissection are not its descendants, so each is excluded separately when dissection is stated absent. HPO has no pulmonary artery dissection term.

stroke or ischemic organ infarction.note: Composite: Stroke (EXACT 'Cerebrovascular accident'; Ischemic stroke and Transient ischemic attack are children), Cerebral infarct (not under Stroke), Hepatic infarction and Splenic infarction for the abdominal-organ infarctions the quotes name. HPO has no renal or mesenteric infarction term; Intestinal ischemia is not used because ischemia without infarction is broader than the item. Myocardial infarction is not listed because the item's sources concern stroke and abdominal organs.

pulmonary hypertension.note: Elevated pulmonary artery pressure: HPO has no term named 'pulmonary hypertension'; this term is the parent of Pre-capillary (with Pulmonary arterial hypertension), Post-capillary and Combined pulmonary hypertension. Pulmonary venous hypertension is not under it, so it is excluded separately.

ventricular hypertrophy.note: Ventricular hypertrophy; exact name match. Left, right and biventricular hypertrophy are children.

hyperextensible or lax skin (cutis laxa).note: Abnormally lax or hyperextensible skin, an exact name match for the composite, parent of Cutis laxa and Hyperextensible skin. It also covers Excessive wrinkled skin, Increased number of skin folds and similar, so its absence would overstate; only Cutis laxa (EXACT 'Lax skin') and Hyperextensible skin (EXACT 'Stretchable skin') are excluded.

joint hypermobility.note: Joint hypermobility; exact name match. Generalized, small- and large-joint hypermobility are children.

joint contractures.note: Joint contracture (EXACT 'Contracture'); Flexion contracture, Congenital contracture and Limb joint contracture are descendants.

diaphragmatic or hiatal (sliding) hernia.note: Composite: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (EXACT 'Diaphragmatic hernia') and Hiatus hernia (EXACT 'Hiatal hernia'; a sliding hernia is a hiatal hernia type, no separate term). Neither is under the other; their common parent Hernia is broader.

pectus excavatum or carinatum.note: Composite: Pectus excavatum and Pectus carinatum. Abnormal sternum morphology carries the EXACT synonym 'Pectus excavatum or carinatum' but is broader (bifid sternum, sternal hypoplasia and others), so observed is null and only the two components are excluded.

scoliosis or kyphoscoliosis.note: Scoliosis; Kyphoscoliosis is its child, so one term covers both.

arachnodactyly.note: Arachnodactyly; exact name match (EXACT 'Long slender fingers', matching the series' 'long, thin fingers').

respiratory distress or insufficiency.note: Composite: Respiratory distress (under Dyspnea) and Respiratory insufficiency (children include Neonatal respiratory distress, Respiratory failure and, via Respiratory failure requiring assisted ventilation, Acute respiratory distress syndrome). Neither is an ancestor of the other; no single term covers both.
